Theresa — thank you, great questions. Attached is a concise MAP and a proposed benchmark plan (FT-058_MAP_v1.pdf). High-level summary below; full plan attached.

MAP / evaluation summary (short):
- Objectives: validate TTFT, end-to-end token latency (p50/p95/p99), sustained throughput and burst tolerance for your payment flow prompts at representative token lengths (avg. 120 tokens output).
- Acceptance criteria (initial):
  • Steady-state: sustain 200 requests/sec (rps) for 1 hour with p95 latency <= 250ms and TTFT p95 <= 150ms.
  • Burst: tolerate spikes up to 900 concurrent requests for short windows (<= 5 minutes) with graceful degradation (queueing and token-based throttles) and no more than 1% 5xx or fatal errors.
  • Degradation policy: when concurrency exceeds safe thresholds, we prefer backpressure (queuing + 429s at route level) rather than silent slowdowns; provide explicit fallback to smaller model variant for degraded tail latencies.

Test plan highlights:
- Load harness: we’ll run 3 phases using your sample prompts via our k6/Gatling harness integrated with Redwood’s tracing.
  1) Ramp & warmup (cache warming, KV pre-load).
  2) Steady-state soak (target rps/concurrency for 60 minutes).
  3) Burst probes (rapid step increases to peak concurrency with short holds).
- Metrics captured: TTFT (first token), per-token throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, rate-limited responses (429) and 5xx counts, CPU/GPU utilization, and per-request token count.
- Queueing model: we’ll measure request queue latency distribution and correlate with backend queue sizes; we expect queueing to appear before 5xx if configured correctly.

Rate-limit tuning suggestions (quick):
- Token-based token_bucket per-route limiter (tokens = in+out tokens) to keep long-output requests from saturating slots.
- Burst window: short token-burst allowance with a cooldown (60s) and a hard concurrency cap.
- Canary policy: start canary at 20% traffic, run burst probe at 50% traffic to validate degradation path.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Day 0: sign MAP (this email thread + attached MAP).
- Day 2: test harness + sample runs (we’ll send initial CSV).
- Day 5: consolidated run results + recommendations.
- Day 10: final recommendations & canary plan for production rollout.

I’ve attached FT-058_MAP_v1.pdf and will run an initial probe this week. If this looks good, please sign off and we’ll schedule the run.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel

Looping in a couple of internal notes for the test plan:

- Warmup & KV cache: make sure we include a dedicated warmup phase that primes KV cache on all serving instances. For short bursts, a cold cache can look like a spike in TTFT that confuses the customer.
- Token budgeting: recommend capping output to 160 tokens in the steady-state tests and adding a small sample of 320-token outputs in burst runs to see token-driven head-of-line effects.
- Model variants: test with primary model (redwood-edu-3b-q4) and a trimmed variant (redwood-edu-3b-q4-small) so fallback is validated.
- Observability hooks: add a per-request route tag so we can correlate Grafana traces to the MAP run IDs.

I’ll help ship the harness config and a recommended rate-limit policy (example: 600 concurrency soft cap, 750 hard cap for bursts with token-bucket decay=60s).

Ran the first probe today — attaching raw CSV (concurrency-run1-results.csv) and a quick summary:

Quick results summary (run 1):
- Steady-state scenario (target 200 rps sustained for 60m): achieved 250 rps average; p95 latency = 180ms; TTFT p95 = 120ms; GPU utilization ~68% across pool.
- Burst probes: stepped to concurrency ~400/600/900 with 60s holds. Observable behavior:
  • Up to 600 concurrency: graceful queueing, p95 latency increased ~1.8x but error rate <0.4%.
  • At 900 concurrency: queue depth spiked and we observed ~2.1% 429s and small number of 5xx (0.15%).
- Observed head-of-line impact from 320-token outputs: a small fraction (~0.6%) of long outputs drove tail-latency for concurrent short calls.

Immediate recommendations:
1) Surface a token-aware soft throttle at 600 concurrency (slot reservations; long outputs consume additional slot weight).
2) Use fallback to the trimmed model variant when queue depth crosses threshold X (we measured X ~= 120 requests queued per node).
3) Tune token-bucket refill = 30–60s depending on expected burst patterns.

I’ve uploaded Grafana snapshots to the MAP dashboard and attached the CSV. Next step: run a second probe that emulates real client arrival patterns (Poisson) and validate canary with 20% traffic.

Rishi
Perf Engineer — Redwood Inference

Theresa — sharing the initial probe results and clear next steps. See attached benchmark-summary-20261123.pdf for charts and the CSV for raw samples. Short summary below.

What we ran: warmup + 60m steady-state at target 200 rps, then three burst probes (60s holds at 400/600/900 concurrency). We captured TTFT, per-token throughput, and queue depths.

Key takeaways:
- Steady-state: comfortably meets acceptance for a baseline (p95 <= 250ms). We saw p95 = 180ms, TTFT p95 = 120ms at 250 rps average.
- Burst handling: graceful up to ~600 concurrency with queueing; at ~900 concurrency we observed degraded behavior (2.1% 429s, 0.15% 5xx). Head-of-line effects present for long outputs (320 tokens) but rare.

Proposed changes before canary:
- Rate-limit policy: soft cap 600 concurrency, hard cap 750; token-weighted slots where each 100 output tokens = 1 extra weight.
- Fallback: auto-switch to redwood-edu-3b-q4-small when queue depth per-node > 120.
- Canary: start at 20% traffic next week; we’ll run a short burst probe at 50% traffic to validate strategy.

Required sign-off (simple thumbs-up):
1) MAP + benchmark as-is and proceed to canary (20% traffic).
2) Need to book Dedicated capacity (monthly commit) if you want to remove the soft cap and guarantee headroom — we can provide numbers and pricing.

Next actions: Jackson, can you confirm a 2-hour window next Tue for canary start? Theresa, if you approve we’ll schedule and share the detailed runbook.

Thanks — Monica
